etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin autographum, in turn from Ancient Greek αὐτόγραφον (autógraphon, “a writing in one’s own hand”). Equivalent to auto- +‎ -graph.

definitions.definition: A person’s own handwriting, especially the signature of a famous or admired person.
(by extension, colloquial) A person's signature used as a mark of formal approval.
A manuscript in the author’s handwriting.
Written in the author’s own handwriting.
(art) Made by the artist himself or herself; authentic.

quote.citation: 1979, Nancy L Pressly, The Fuseli Circle in Rome, Yale Center for British Art, p. 37:
quote.text: Schiff  […]  believes most of the drawings are autograph.

quote.citation: 1992, Malise Forbes Adam, Mary Mauchline, edited by Wendy Wassyng Roworth, Angelica Kauffman, Reaktion Books, published 1992, page 116:
quote.text: Not surprisingly, he attributed to Kauffman two important works that are no longer accepted as autograph.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To sign, or write one’s name or signature on a book etc
(transitive) To write something in one's own handwriting
